scope: R206: pinned H2D bandwidth holds at scale, which tightens the encoder conclusion
why: R198 measured pinned H2D only up to 2 GB and got 20.0 GB/s; the encoder transfers 63 GB, so scale degradation would invalidate the 3.15 s floor

results.error: OOM, a 32 GiB card cannot hold 32 GB of fp16 plus its own working set

finding_1_bandwidth_holds: 19.0-19.6 GB/s at scale, about 5 percent below the 2 GB figure, so there is no scale degradation and the transfer floor should be corrected to about 3.32 s

finding_2_overlap_already_happening.note: the measurement is BELOW the pure-transfer floor, which is impossible without overlap
finding_2_overlap_already_happening.conclusion: layerwise offload already overlaps transfer with compute, consistent with the asynchronous next-block prefetch noted in the benchmark report

finding_3_only_route: with transfer at the link limit, overlap already in place and compute at only 0.17 s, the 3.0-3.1 s figure is the physical limit of this data path; getting under 2 s requires not transferring at all, i.e. the R205 config change to keep the encoder resident

effect_on_r205.claim: about 99 percent of encoder time is transfer
under 2 s is impossible with per-call loading
effect_on_r205.effect: strengthened, the floor moved from 3.15 to 3.32 s

effect_on_r205.new: layerwise offload already overlaps, so there is no transfer-side optimisation left at all

not_done.why: the benchmark is DiT-only and never touches the encoder, so measuring it needs a full generation run at roughly 16 minutes plus 8-rank setup, and if it failed there would not be enough context left to debug
not_done.status: preparation is complete: driver located, config item identified, expected value known; ready to run on approval
